content:
alex: pasted the nsys timeline here — can someone sanity-check? I see a cluster of small kernels but big memcpy spikes that look like they block downstream kernels. timeline: https://img.internal/abc123.png
maria: yep saw it. looks like copies on copy engine are serialized with kernels on the same GPU? hard to tell without stream labels. can you upload the trace (.qdrep) or run `nsys stats`?
alex: uploaded `trace.qdrep` to the shared folder, link in the trace. quick notes: workload is KV-prefetch during decoding, batch size 8, seq len ~64, model uses quantized kernels.
jt: quick read — those big horizontal bands around 0.15s are host->device copies on the copy engine. kernels run on stream 1, memcpy on stream 2, but CUDA's default scheduling + our host thread pinning means memcpy ends up serialized because host thread is preempted. CPU scheduling gaps show a ~40ms hole coincident with memcpy start.
ryan: +1. Also check whether the memcpy is using pinned memory. If it's falling back to pageable memory, cudaMemcpyAsync will sync under the hood, showing up like a blocking memcpy.
maria: good catch. alex, can you paste the command used to capture the trace? need to see if you passed sampling for OS threads.
alex: ran `nsys profile --output=kvtrace --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=cpu`
nsys-bot: nsys report: copied 12 H2D operations, 4 D2H ops, avg memcpy H2D = 24.8ms, std=6.1ms; kernel avg = 3.2ms
alex: that avg memcpy seems high. memory is pinned — we allocate a staging buffer with `cudaHostAlloc(..., cudaHostAllocDefault)` before copy.
jt: check flags — `cudaHostAllocDefault` is pinned but not write-combined; try `cudaHostAllocWriteCombined` for streaming uploads. also ensure `cudaMemcpyAsync` calls use distinct streams for different batches so copy engine can overlap.
ryan: another angle: our kernel selection path currently picks an SM-optimized kernel for short sequences — that kernel launches lots of tiny kernels which increases kernel launch overhead and fragmentation. small kernels + large memcpys can interleave poorly. maybe prefer fewer larger kernels for seq < 128.
maria: I noticed KV prefetch issues: prefetch loop does `for shard in shards: cudaMemcpyAsync(prefetch_buf[shard], ...); cudaStreamSynchronize(stream)` in some code paths — that sync kills concurrency. confirm?
alex: oh wow that's in the legacy path. I'll grep.
alex: confirmed — a leftover `cudaStreamSynchronize(stream)` in the prefetch hotpath when a retry flag is set. removing it might help.
ryan: great find. even an accidental sync once per batch can collapse overlap. also consider switching to per-shard NVTX ranges so we can see which sub-ops dominate.
jt: suggested quick experiments: 1) remove the sync + re-run trace. 2) ensure host buffer uses `cudaHostAllocWriteCombined` and `cudaMemcpyAsync` to a non-default stream. 3) run with `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx --cuda-memory-usage=true -o kv2`
ci-bot: perf job queued: job 8234 for branch `kv-prefetch-fix`
maria: small note on CPU scheduling gaps — our server runs other highest-priority threads (logging/agent) on the same cpus as the host copy threads. pin H2D copy threads to isolated cores to avoid preemption spikes. see `taskset`/cgroups change in the infra runbook.
alex: running experiments now, will post new trace in ~30m. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
ryan: if new trace still shows memcpy hotspots, we should also run `nvprof --print-gpu-trace` to get more per-kernel metrics; nsys sometimes aggregates.
jt: agree. and once we have a clean trace, we should add a microbenchmark to CI that simulates KV prefetch (varying seq len and batch) so regressions don't sneak in.
alex: noted. leaving this thread open — will update with the new qdrep and `nsys stats` output.
